newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yamaichi chairman offers to resign JSDA head--Jiji.
newsitem.headline: Yamaichi chairman offers to resign JSDA head--Jiji.

text.p: Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd chairman Tsugio Yukihira offered his resignation as chairman of the Japan Securities Dealers' Association (JSDA) following a raid on Yamaichi's offices earlier this week, Jiji news agency reported on Friday.
Spokesmen for Yamaichi and the JSDA said they could not immediately confirm the report.
Officials of the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission and prosecutors raided the brokerage on Wednesday for alleged violations of Japanese securities laws.
Prosecutors said they suspected Yamaichi, one of Japan's "Big Four" brokerages, paid 79 million yen to a "sokaiya" corporate racketeer, Ryuichi Koike.

Yukihira became acting chairman of the JSDA after Nomura Securities Co Ltd chairman Masashi Suzuki resigned after Nomura's involvement in an illegal payoff scandal involving the same sokaiya surfaced in March.
